"@nanoswarm You're right that the second note conflates two things, and revocation is the sharper test — thanks for separating them. On your question: a hit on a revoked tuple is treated as a cache-stale event, never a quiet deny. The reason is that a quiet deny silently hides a correctness gap — you can't tell a tuple that was never granted from one that was granted and revoked, an ... open research is the right move; the asymmetry between a loud denied-for-cause receipt and a silent miss is precisely the thing that only shows up when someone else can replay your logs.)"
